WIT Fire Detection Project - Nano Every

Detects various fire stimuli and performs alarm functions accordingly

BJJ138IhGg.content: Heat detection is using some combination of components to monitor for a fire event.

H1CX4OLsGe.content: Enter alarm state if manual pull OR if the temperature is greater than the threshold.

BkhjmwLsGx.description: Reads the analog output from the AD8495 K-type thermocouple amplifier.
BkhjmwLsGx.label: Thermocouple

Bkgxns7vUifl.content: When the sampling rate clock ticks, take an analog voltage reading from the thermocouple module.

B1WlnjXD8jMl.content:
Convert from volts to temperature.

Temperature °C = (Vout - 1.25)/0.005

= (Vout - 1.25) * 200

H1Mx2omD8sfg.content: The output from the analog-read block is a percentage of the full scale voltage (5V max), so multiply the output by 5 to get Vout.

ryQlhj7P8szg.content: If the temperature is greater than the specified value, set to TRUE.

HJ3gVD8szl.description: Reads the analog output from the NTC thermistor voltage divider.
HJ3gVD8szl.label: Thermistor

Hk-g2eEPUsMe.content: When the sampling rate clock ticks, take an analog voltage reading from the thermistor.

rkfg3gEw8oMg.content: The output from the analog-read block is a percentage of the full scale voltage (5V max), so multiply the output by 5 to get Vout.

rJ7xhg4v8jMl.content:
If the voltage is less than the specified value, output TRUE. Since this thermistor is a negative temp coeff, we need to use a less than comparison.

1.32V corresponds to 50°C using the complex equation for NTC thermistors which would take too many blocks to calculate out.

H1VxhgVDUjzg.content: This gate is needed so that on initial boot, we don't go right to the alarm state due to the thermistor value being undetermined. So only after the first ADC read is complete do we allow the less than block output to pass to the OR gate.

BysENDLjMg.description: Reads the analog output from the linear wire detector voltage divider.
BysENDLjMg.label: LWD

BJ-xsNVPLsfl.content: When the sampling rate clock ticks, take an analog voltage reading from the LWD.

rkfeo4VPIife.content: The output from the analog-read block is a percentage of the full scale voltage (5V max), so multiply the output by 5 to get Vout.

rkQeiNEvUoMx.content:
If the voltage is less than the specified value, output TRUE. Since this linear wire is a short when activated, we need to use a less than comparison.

4.8k nominal resistance results in 1.62V, so use 1V for some margin.

Bk4xsNVv8izx.content: This gate is needed so that on initial boot, we don't go right to the alarm state due to the analog value being undetermined. So only after the first ADC read is complete do we allow the less than block output to pass to the OR gate.

SJYYVLLhfg.content: Flip flop is used to change states between "Fire Not Detected (or SYSTEM READY)" and "Fire Detected". The manual pull or temperature exceeding the threshold transitions the system to the Fire Detected state. The system reset button transitions the system to the Fire Not Detected state.
